title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from The Principal Grapes
objectives: Recognise the eight principal grapes by their flavours
Explain how varieties are propagated and labelled
Predict a wine's style from grape and climate

steps.prompt: Match each grape to a typical aroma.
steps.explanation: Each grape has a signature you can learn to recognise.

steps.prompt: Why are vineyards planted with cuttings rather than seeds?
options: Vines don't breed true from seed
steps.explanation: A seedling would be a new variety. Cuttings keep every vine identical to the parent.

steps.prompt: Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris are the same grape.
steps.explanation: Yes. The Italian name usually signals a light, crisp style; the French name a richer, rounder one.

steps.prompt: Which grapes are normally deeply coloured and tannic?
steps.explanation: Cabernet and Syrah have thick skins. Pinot Noir is pale and low in tannin, and Riesling is white.

steps.prompt: Merlot ripens ____ than Cabernet Sauvignon, which helps in cooler years.
steps.explanation: Merlot ripens about two weeks earlier, so it is the safer half of a Bordeaux blend in a cool year.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Eight grapes cover most wine: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Pinot Grigio, Cabernet, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Syrah
Varieties are copied by cuttings and named on varietal labels
Grape gives the character; climate gives the ripeness
